thesis: AI coding assistant pilots stall around day 90 because teams measure seat activation instead of changed work, so the renewal decision arrives with no evidence either way.

anecdotes.summary: Hook and frame: CFO asks what changed, 92% activation slide.
Two-team fintech pilot; week-one review-turnaround metric made renewal case.

claims.statement: Halvorsen Research interviewed 32 companies for its May 2026 report on platform teams and AI tooling. The median pilot ran 94 days before a renewal decision.
9 of those 32 companies tracked any change in cycle time or review load during the pilot. All 9 renewed. The other 23 tracked only seat activation. 11 of them renewed.
In the Northfield Developer Survey 2026 (n=1,240 developers, fielded March 2026), 61% said their company's assistant pilot had "no agreed success measure" at launch.
In the Northfield Developer Survey 2026, weekly active use in pilots with no success measure fell from 78% in month one to 41% by month three. In pilots that had one, it went from 80% to 66%.
A 2025 Ostrava University study of 400 pull requests found no measurable change in review time with assistant use.
It's one study, 400 pull requests, and one metric.
In Halvorsen Research's 2026 report, 11 of the 23 companies that tracked only seat activation renewed.
